items.title: Home
items.text: Immich ReverseGeo is a self-hosted companion for immich that improves location names when the built-in results feel too broad, too generic, or simply wrong for your library.  Get started Installation GitHub

items.title: Check a coordinate before processing
items.text: Open Lookup, paste coordinates from a photo you know, and inspect the country, state, city, and matching sources before running against your library. Lookup previews location names without updating Immich assets; it may download country data when needed.

items.title: What it can help with
items.text:
• Missing or overly broad location names on photos that already have GPS coordinates.
  • Matching around coastlines, islands, administrative boundaries, and airport areas.
  • Repeatable processing with locally cached geographic data.

Results depend on the available source data. It cannot add missing GPS coordinates or guarantee a better name for every point. Compare known locations in Lookup first, then choose the settings that fit your library.

To correct existing names, use Location Management to scan your photos, review proposed differences, and apply only the changes you select. Back up the database before applying. Saved scans let you continue unfinished work; Change History records applied names and supports undo when the metadata has not changed. See Correct existing location names.

See Using the App for the workflow and Data Sources for coverage and licence limits.

items.title: Before You Run It On Real Data
items.text:
• It needs direct access to your immich database.
  • immich's own reverse geocoding should be turned off first.
  • It writes back to immich metadata.
  • It can clear existing immich location values from the Data page.
  • It needs internet access the first time it downloads extra data for a country.
  • Large country downloads can consume hundreds of megabytes each.

Turn off immich's built-in reverse geocoding

Immich ReverseGeo writes city, state, and country back into immich.

If immich's own reverse geocoding remains enabled, both systems can overwrite the same fields and step on each other's results.

Disable immich's built-in reverse geocoding before running Immich ReverseGeo. See immich's official docs: Reverse Geocoding and Reverse Geocoding Settings.

Back up your immich database first

Immich ReverseGeo reads from and writes to immich's database.

Before running processing on real assets, and before clearing existing location fields, create a proper immich backup first: Backup and Restore | Immich

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
You do not need to understand the internals to use Immich ReverseGeo, but the overall shape is simple: the app reads coordinates from immich, matches them against built-in and downloaded location data, and writes the final place names back.

For a plain-language explanation of the active geographic data sources, see Data Sources.

items.title: Main components
items.text:
Web app

The web UI handles settings, processing, coordinate lookups, country caches, location reviews, saved scans, change history, and logs.

Built-in data

Country matching and airport matching are available right away from data shipped with the app.

Downloaded country data

Extra per-country data is downloaded when needed so state and city matching can be more precise.

items.title: Processing pipeline
items.text:
The background processor:

  1. reads unprocessed assets from immich
  2. resolves bundled country
  3. resolves administrative areas from cached Overture divisions and optionally cached GADM country packages
  4. optionally queries bundled airport infrastructure
  5. writes city/state/country back to immich when a complete result is available

items.title: Reviewing existing names
items.text:
Location Management uses the same location matching to scan assets with GPS coordinates, including those with existing names. Scanning saves the existing and proposed names without changing Immich. You can reopen saved results or continue unfinished scans later.

Applying selected differences writes the exact reviewed names directly, after checking that the existing names and coordinates still match the snapshot. Change History records previous names and outcomes, with undo available when the applied metadata has not changed. These records live under /data, so preserve that volume across container replacements. They do not replace an Immich database backup.

See Location Management for the review, confirmation, and recovery steps.

items.title: Active data sourcesBuilt inDownloaded on demandOptional live lookup help
items.text:
Country matching data and airport matching data are included in the app image.

Country-specific Overture and optional GADM data is downloaded locally when needed for better state and city matching.

The Lookup page can also show live Overture Places diagnostics when you want to inspect a point more deeply.

items.title: Changelog
items.text:
This is the public-facing release summary for Immich ReverseGeo.

Technical implementation notes live in CHANGELOG.md.

items.title: Unreleased
items.text:
• Lookup now reports an incomplete result when a required country cache cannot be prepared, instead of suggesting that a country-only fallback would be written. Retry after resolving the cache error.

  • Choose English, local/source names, or a preferred language in Settings. Lookup, correction previews, and processing use available Overture translations, including parent-area names. Older country caches rebuild once to retain alternate names. Existing Immich names stay unchanged until you apply reviewed changes or reprocess them. See Location name language.

This release adds selected location corrections and guarded undo, resumable scans, clearer reviews, and improved administrative matching.

  • Outdated Overture country caches refresh automatically when used. If an update fails, the app keeps a compatible previous cache and retries later. Check known coordinates in Lookup before applying changed names.
  • Overture cache preparation now shows separate query and cache-building stages. A query percentage describes that stage, not the entire download.

  • Fixed stable Docker image promotion and added recovery for an already-built release image.

  • Updated the app guide with current screenshots and the quick-start correction workflow. Added help for slow cache preparation, memory limits, and handled scan differences.

  • Location reviews keep selection actions within reach and move keyboard focus into and back from confirmation. Saved Scans and Change History can filter unfinished or pending work across all pages. Navigation and comparison tables work on smaller screens.
  • Settings shows schedules in UTC, previews the next run in your browser's timezone, validates changes before saving, and displays effective processing limits. The save bar stays available while scrolling.
  • Scans show checked totals and estimated remaining processing time. Highlighted characters make spelling, punctuation, and invisible differences visible in both existing and proposed names.
  • Exact administrative boundary matches now take priority over neighbouring tolerance-only matches. Overture parent names prefer English when available; re-download an older country cache and check Lookup before applying corrections.
  • Country-cache preparation shows its current stage and elapsed time, with file-transfer or estimated query progress when available. Query progress is not a percentage of the whole cache; see cache preparation.
  • Scripts can start a processing pass with POST /api/processing/run. The endpoint needs no API key, so keep it private like the web UI. An accepted response does not mean processing succeeded; see scripted runs.

  • Logs has a Follow logs toggle and a panel that fills the available page height. Connection recovery explains how to continue saved scans and check interrupted changes. Browser favicons are clearer at small sizes.

  • Continue unfinished scans from Saved Scans after closing the page or restarting the app. The app restores the original options, keeps earlier results, and resumes after the last saved asset. Saved reports also show pause status and recorded progress.

  • Scans that reach their difference limit now show a clear Paused for review notice and a Continue Scan button that stays visible while reviewing results.
  • Show only different values is enabled by default in live and saved scans. Unchanged results no longer load photo previews, even when you choose to show them.
  • Applying a batch now clears it from Ready to apply so you can review the next differences. Use Applied, Needs attention, or All results to inspect saved outcomes without applying the same snapshot again.
  • Added Location Management: scan and review names, apply selected corrections from live or saved scans, and use Change History to inspect results or undo unchanged applied metadata. Section tabs highlight the current page; history shows clear result counts and remaining undo work. Previous preview links still work. See Using the App and the technical changelog.

This first versioned release brings location previews, improved country and city matching, refreshed airport data, and lower retained country-boundary memory. Earlier development milestones remain listed below.

  • Country lookup uses less memory, with a low-memory mode for smaller hosts and automatic release of idle country boundaries after five minutes. An optional bounded cache can retain recently used boundaries. These settings do not cap total app memory; see memory settings.

  • Optionally fill a missing city with a point-only airport within 100 m. The new setting defaults off and never replaces a resolved city or county.

  • By default, airport names now require a mapped boundary matching the photo coordinates, with a 5 m tolerance for minor GPS or mapping differences. Nearby airports outside that tolerance are excluded. Point-only airports can fill a missing city only when the optional 100 m fallback is enabled; use Lookup to inspect excluded airport candidates.

  • Use county names as a fallback for US photos where Overture has no preferred city-like match, instead of falling back directly to a state or a nearby airport.

  • Refresh the built-in airport data. Use Lookup to compare airport matches before reprocessing existing photos.

  • Country detection now keeps supported territories as their own country identity instead of replacing them with the administering country.

  • Fixed the reported Hong Kong coordinates and expanded built-in coverage for Macao, Greenland, the Faroe Islands, Jersey, Guernsey, the Isle of Man, Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Bermuda, Gibraltar, the Cayman Islands, the British Virgin Islands, Aruba, Curaçao, the Åland Islands, Réunion, French Polynesia, and New Caledonia.
  • Older custom country databases remain readable without modification. Incorrect identities in newer-format databases produce a clear mapping error.

  • Country detection still works offline from bundled data. Use Lookup to verify a coordinate and inspect the later Overture and optional GADM results before processing your library.

  • Optional GADM lookup can now use Hong Kong and Macao administrative data from its China download, preserving each territory's country name. Processing uses the related/shared package setting.

  • Apply the existing small country-boundary tolerance to points just outside a country polygon's bounding box, while keeping exact country matches preferred.

  • Keep overlapping area choices consistent when otherwise equal matches arrive in a different order.

  • Lookup now explains whether no country boundary matched or a matched boundary has an unresolved country code.

  • The Dashboard now explains which photos a run processes and how to correct existing names.

  • Added Preview Location Corrections under Data. Compare existing and proposed names before resetting selected photos. Preview leaves Immich data unchanged; see Using the App.

  • Added checks for future bundled country-data updates. The shipped geographic data and country-matching behavior are unchanged by this tooling update.

  • Include version details, integrity checksums, and signed build provenance with downloadable release packages, along with the bundled geographic data needed by the app.

  • Country selection lists now use bundled names consistently across platforms. This change does not add geographic coverage or change how coordinates match a country.

  • Nearby Places filters now avoid unrelated sports and transport businesses that previously matched part of a category name.

  • Make the website easier to read in light and dark mode. Follow your system theme by default and remember your choice when you switch modes.

  • Lookup now shows Nearby Places as an investigation tool, with several suggestions, distances, categories, sources, and reasons for inclusion or exclusion. Nearby places do not change the location written to Immich.

  • Improved downloaded administrative coverage for Saba, Sint Eustatius, Clipperton Island, and Jan Mayen. Affected older caches refresh automatically when needed; other country caches remain usable.

  • Restored optional live Places lookup compatibility with recent Overture releases.

  • New Overture country downloads can use parent areas to improve city matching and keep city/state results consistent. Existing caches remain usable; re-download a country cache and test known coordinates in Lookup to use the improvement.

  • Overture download failures now report release-discovery problems instead of trying an expired data release.

  • Fixed the app stopping while waiting for an infrequent custom schedule, such as an annual run.

  • Docker releases now have version tags for controlled upgrades. GitHub's designated latest stable release updates latest; older release retries and prereleases do not automatically change it. edge continues to follow development builds.

  • Development images now publish only after their build and automated checks pass.

  • You can now reuse Immich's DB_HOSTNAME setting to connect to an external database. Existing DB_HOST settings continue to work and take precedence when nonblank.

  • Dashboard and Logs now show dates and times in your browser's timezone. Downloaded logs remain in UTC with full dates.

This release fixes the app running out of memory and restarting during processing.

  • Fixed the container growing in memory until it was killed, then restarting mid-run. Country matching was doing far more geometry work than it needed to on almost every photo. See issue #13.
  • Country matching is also much faster. On typical European coordinates a country lookup went from roughly 2.5 ms to under 0.1 ms.
  • The installation snippet now sets a mem_limit of 2 GB. Existing installations can add this to their Compose file to limit total container memory. No extra runtime memory-tuning settings are required. Larger country caches or higher parallelism may need a higher limit. See The container keeps restarting or gets killed.
  • In rare cases near a border, a photo that sits exactly inside one country but within about 16 m of a neighbour now always resolves to the country it is actually in. Previously the neighbour could win.

This release focuses on better administrative area matching and clearer data management.

  • Optional GADM support can now be enabled as an extra source for state and city matching. Use Lookup first to compare Overture and GADM results, then enable it for processing if it improves your library. See GADM administrative areas.
  • Lookup now shows what it is doing while it runs, including when it is downloading or waiting for country data.
  • The Data area now has one administrative cache table for downloaded Overture and GADM data. It shows the data source, country, row count, version, size, download time, and cache actions. See Data tools.
  • Split-territory GADM fallbacks can help in places where one country match may need related packages, such as Denmark with Greenland and the Faroe Islands, or the UK with Jersey, Guernsey, and the Isle of Man.
  • A new Data Sources page explains where the geographic data comes from, what each source is used for, what is built in or downloaded, and the important license notes.
  • The reset page is now called Reset Immich Geo Data so it is clearer that it changes Immich reverse geo fields, not just this app's local cache.

• Added the City Resolver page so you can see the bundled defaults, change the global city matching behavior, and add per-country overrides when a country needs different city-like divisions.
  • Added curated bundled country defaults for places where the normal city matching order needs a different preference.

• Added an option to turn off airport matching if you prefer normal city or commune names.
  • Added the Reset Immich Geo Data page so you can clear reverse geo city, state, and country values before rerunning processing.
• Initial Version.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
The Settings page is intentionally small. Most users only need to check the database connection, pick a schedule, and tune how aggressively processing should run. Country-specific city matching now lives on its own City Resolver page.

For manual runs, coordinate testing, and reset tools, see Using the App.

items.title: Database settings
items.text:
Database values are environment-backed and shown as read-only in the UI.

The app reads:

  • DB_HOSTNAME (or the existing DB_HOST setting)
  • DB_PORT
  • DB_USERNAME
  • DB_PASSWORD
  • DB_DATABASE_NAME

These values are required because the app reads and updates Immich data directly. Passwords containing semicolons, quotes, or spaces are supported; pass the exact password through DB_PASSWORD, following your container or host environment's quoting rules.

For the database host, a nonblank DB_HOST takes precedence over DB_HOSTNAME. If neither has a nonblank value, the host defaults to database. You can reuse Immich's DB_HOSTNAME value for an external database without renaming it.

Read-only by design

The database values shown in the UI come from the running environment and are there as a sanity check, not for editing.

Keep them in Docker or your host environment

Set the database values where you launch the app, then restart it if you change them.

items.title: Saving settings
items.text:
Settings and City Resolver show whether changes are saved. Save changes saves the values present when you click it. If you keep editing during a save, those later edits stay pending for another save. Leaving an editor with unsaved changes asks for confirmation.

The save bar stays available as you scroll. Settings validates enabled schedules and processing limits before saving; correct the displayed error before trying again. Saved expressions that do not fit a preset remain in Advanced custom schedule, including invalid values. Invalid enabled schedules must be corrected before saving; they are not automatically clamped to a different schedule.

The two editors save their own sections, so saving City Resolver does not overwrite processing or schedule changes made elsewhere. Test Connection checks the environment-backed database connection without saving settings.

Saving replaces the settings file only after the new values have been written completely. If a save fails, the previous file remains available. Database credentials stay in the environment.

items.title: Photo previews and Immich links
items.text:
Live location previews and saved reports can show photo thumbnails and an Open in Immich link. This connection is optional; location processing still uses your database settings.

Add these environment variables to the Immich ReverseGeo service, then recreate or restart it:

Variable Purpose IMMICH_URL Immich server URL reachable from Immich ReverseGeo, such as http://immich-server:2283. IMMICH_WEB_URL Optional URL used by your browser, such as https://photos.example.com. Defaults to IMMICH_URL. IMMICH_API_KEY Immich API key with asset.view permission and access to the photos being previewed. 
environment:
  IMMICH_URL: http://immich-server:2283
  IMMICH_WEB_URL: https://photos.example.com
  IMMICH_API_KEY: ${REVERSEGEO_IMMICH_API_KEY}

Put REVERSEGEO_IMMICH_API_KEY in your compose environment or secrets-backed deployment configuration. The key stays on the server and is not stored in settings or saved reports. An API key can only show photos its Immich account can access; a database-wide preview may include photos belonging to other users.

You can configure only IMMICH_WEB_URL if you want original-photo links without thumbnails. Thumbnails are fetched on demand for assets in saved preview reports and are not saved as image files. Missing thumbnails, denied access, or an unavailable Immich server show Preview unavailable while the saved location results remain usable. Original-photo links open Immich in a new tab and use your normal Immich sign-in.

items.title: Processing settings
items.text:
The Settings page lets you control:

  • whether processing runs automatically
  • when it runs, using simple presets or a custom cron expression
  • batch size, delay, and parallelism
  • low-memory mode for hosts with limited RAM
  • how long country boundaries stay cached in RAM when idle
  • whether a mapped airport boundary containing the coordinate can override the city name
  • whether GADM administrative areas are enabled as an optional source
  • whether GADM should be preferred over cached Overture divisions
  • whether split-territory GADM fallback families should be tried
  • whether every asset is written to the log

Most users should stay on the preset schedule options. Custom cron expressions can also schedule infrequent runs, such as once per year. Manual runs from the dashboard still work even when automatic scheduling is disabled.

All schedule times use UTC. Settings previews the next occurrence in your browser's timezone; local clock changes do not change the UTC schedule. The preview reflects your current edits and applies only after saving. Memory tuning, batch size, pause between batches, and parallel workers are under Advanced Processing Limits. The page shows effective batch and worker limits, including low-memory overrides.

See the schedule and processing settings

Schedule

Choose when the app should run automatically, from simple presets up to a custom cron schedule.

Batch size

Controls how many photos are processed at a time before the next pause or write cycle.

Parallelism

Controls how much work the app does at once. Higher values can be faster, but they also put more load on the system and database.

Airport matching

Leave it on if airport names are useful to you. Turn it off if you prefer commune or city names for photos taken on airport grounds.

Optional GADM source

You can enable GADM as an extra administrative boundary source, either as a fallback behind Overture or as the preferred admin source.

items.title: Airport matching
items.text:
When enabled, airport matching uses an airport name only if the coordinate falls inside its mapped polygon boundary or within 5 m of its edge. This small tolerance accommodates minor GPS and mapping differences. Point-only airports are excluded by default. Airports with missing or invalid boundaries are excluded. A nearby airport or overlapping bounding box is not enough, even when the city is missing; the app keeps the administrative result and its usual state/country fallback.

Use Lookup to check a known airport photo and a nearby photo first. The airport trace distinguishes a boundary match with the 5 m tolerance, outside boundary, and boundary unavailable. Missing or inaccurate polygons can prevent airport matching. Turn airport matching off if you prefer city or commune names. Existing Immich names are not rewritten automatically; use Location Management to scan, review, and apply selected corrections.

items.title: Optional point-only airport fallback
items.text:
Enable Allow point-only airports within 100 m when no city or county is found under Settings → Processing only if this behavior is useful for your library. It defaults off and also requires airport matching to be enabled.

The fallback uses the nearest airport represented by a valid point within 100 m. It never replaces a resolved administrative city or county, and mapped boundary matches remain preferred. A point record cannot bypass an available boundary for a same-named airport.

Proximity does not confirm the photo was taken on airport grounds. A point may be far from the terminal, so some airport photos still will not match. Missing, invalid, and line geometries do not qualify. Test airport and nearby non-airport photos in Lookup first; it labels this result as an unconfirmed point-only proximity fallback. Review proposed corrections in Location Management before applying them.

items.title: Location name language
items.text:
Under Settings → Processing, choose Location name language:

  • English (default) prefers an available English name, then the source's primary name. Existing settings keep this behavior.
  • Local / source name prefers the primary name supplied by Overture, then English. This can restore names such as Bayern instead of Bavaria. The primary name is a source choice; multilingual areas do not necessarily have one universally preferred local name.
  • Preferred language lets you search by language name or code, such as French (fr). Suggestions show the main languages. You can still enter a regional or script code manually. It tries your language code, then broader forms of that code, then the primary name, then English. For example, fr-CA tries fr-CA, then fr. Other examples include de, ja, and zh-Hant. The language list does not guarantee translated names; availability varies by place. Save your choice and test known coordinates in Lookup before processing.

Save the setting, test familiar coordinates in Lookup, then use Location Management → Scan & Review to compare existing names and apply reviewed changes to selected assets. Changing the language does not rewrite existing Immich metadata. A processing run or preview already in progress keeps its starting settings.

The preference applies to Overture city and state names, including names obtained from parent areas. Local and preferred-language modes also use available Overture country names for the already resolved country or territory. If none is available, the bundled country name remains. The English default keeps the bundled country name. Country codes and geographic matching do not change.

Translations depend on the source data. Missing translations fall back independently for each name, so a result can contain more than one language. GADM administrative names, bundled airport names, and optional Nearby Places suggestions keep their existing source naming behavior. The setting does not change the app's interface language or create missing translations.

Older Overture administrative caches rebuild once when next needed to retain alternate names. The first lookup, preview, or processing request waits for that download. After rebuilding, switching language does not require another download. Cache rebuilding alone does not update Immich metadata.

items.title: Low-memory mode
items.text:
Normal mode uses compact boundary storage automatically, with full coordinate precision. No extra setting or cache download is needed for this reduction.

Enable Low-memory mode under Settings → Processing when RAM is limited, then save before starting a new run.

The mode:

  • processes one asset at a time, in batches of at most 25
  • runs one expensive country download or remote query at a time, shared with Lookup
  • uses one DuckDB worker and a 256 MiB buffer budget for remote queries and Overture cache creation
  • reads matching country polygons from disk instead of retaining the worldwide country index in RAM

The first country lookup prepares a small disk index from the bundled data under /data/country-polygon-parts.db. Later lookups read only nearby polygon parts, including their original boundaries and holes. This requires no network download and rebuilds automatically after bundled data changes. If the index cannot be prepared, the app keeps using the original disk lookup, which can be slower.

Your saved batch size and parallelism stay unchanged and are used again when you disable the mode. Work already in progress finishes with its existing limits; the next processing run uses the new batch and worker limits.

Expect slower processing and more disk reads. This is not a total RAM cap: the web app, geometry checks, and native libraries use additional memory. Temporary DuckDB spill files live under /data/duckdb-tmp. Memory shown by your host may stay elevated after a run while the runtime keeps freed memory available for reuse.

Use Lookup on a few known coordinates first, then compare memory use during a processing pass. Compare the first pass that creates country caches separately from later passes that reuse them. This mode changes resource use, not location matching rules, and does not repair missing or incorrect boundary data.

In both modes, processing checks skipped IDs one batch at a time rather than loading the entire skipped history into RAM.

items.title: Limiting the country boundary cache
items.text:
Enable Limit country boundary cache under Settings → Processing to reduce country matching memory while keeping your normal worker and batch settings. It reads country boundary parts from disk and retains recently used parts, instead of keeping the full prepared country index in RAM. Leave it off for the fastest repeated lookups.

Start with the default 256 MiB budget. Values from 1 to 1024 MiB are supported. A smaller budget causes more disk reads and repeated geometry decoding. Parts larger than the budget are checked without caching them. Save to apply; changing this option or its budget releases the existing country cache.

The budget estimates retained geometry size. It is not a total RAM cap: active lookups, the web app, administrative boundaries, downloads, and native libraries also use memory. Evicted geometry becomes available for garbage collection, so the host's RAM figure may fall later. The idle release setting below also applies to this cache. Low-memory mode takes precedence and does not retain country boundary parts.

Use Lookup on a few known coordinates, then compare memory and processing time on your library. Compare the first pass separately from later passes. This option preserves country matching rules; it cannot repair incorrect or missing boundary data.

items.title: Releasing idle country boundaries
items.text:
Normal mode reads country data directly from disk while building its in-memory index, reducing temporary memory use during loading. The completed index stays cached for fast repeated lookups.

Release country index after idle (minutes) controls normal mode's cached country boundaries. The default is 5 minutes without a country lookup. Use 0 to keep them cached, or a value from 1 to 1440 minutes to release them after idle time. Save the setting to apply it.

Releasing the index makes its memory available for garbage collection; the host's RAM figure may fall later. The next country lookup rebuilds the index, so its first result can take longer. Active country lookups are allowed to finish. Low-memory mode reads from disk and does not retain this index.

Use Lookup on a known coordinate before and after the idle period to check the result and rebuild delay. This setting reduces retained country memory; it is not a total RAM cap and does not repair incorrect location data.

items.title: GADM administrative areas
items.text:
When enabled, GADM adds another country-level administrative boundary source for state and city matching.

Processing and location scans query the preferred source first. If it supplies both state and city, the other source is skipped. Otherwise, the other source fills only missing fields. This can avoid unnecessary country-cache downloads; it cannot repair incorrect names supplied by the preferred source. Lookup still queries both enabled sources so you can compare their results before changing your preference.

Recommended starting point:

  • turn Enable GADM administrative areas on
  • leave Prefer GADM administrative results off at first
  • use Lookup to compare results before making GADM the primary admin source

What it can help with:

  • countries where Overture admin divisions are sparse or pick the wrong city-like name
  • places where a more traditional admin-boundary dataset gives better municipality or state names

What it does not fix by itself:

  • wrong bundled country detection
  • airport names winning when airport matching is still enabled
  • missing places that are not present in either source

items.title: Split-territory fallback families
items.text:
The optional GADM territory fallback setting lets the app try related territory packages or a shared country download. For Hong Kong and Macao, GADM stores administrative boundaries in its China download. The app uses matching boundaries for state and city names while keeping Hong Kong or Macao as the country. These shared-data lookups require a geometry match and skip unnamed subdivisions; a bounding box alone is not enough.

Test the coordinate in Lookup first; its GADM investigation uses the shared download automatically. For processing, enable GADM and leave Try related or shared GADM country packages checked. The first lookup can download the larger China package; Hong Kong and Macao share the resulting cache. This cannot supply subdivisions missing from GADM or repair an unresolved initial country match.

Examples include:

  • Denmark, Greenland, and the Faroe Islands
  • United Kingdom, Jersey, Guernsey, and the Isle of Man

This is a targeted fallback, not a global scan of every possible territory.

items.title: City Resolver
items.text:
The City Resolver page lets you adjust how the app picks a city name when Overture returns several possible matches.

It gives you:

  • bundled default rules that ship with the app
  • an optional global override
  • country-specific overrides
  • a searchable country picker
  • simple up/down controls to change the order of preferred place types from the official Overture list
  • a choice between:
  • prefer the tighter match
  • prefer the broader match

This keeps the main Settings page simple while still giving you a way to fix countries where the default city result is not what you want.

items.title: What it actually changes
items.text:
The City Resolver controls which city-like area the app prefers. When Overture provides parent information for that area, the app also uses it to select a consistent state.

An area that contains the coordinate exactly takes priority over a neighbouring area that matches only through boundary tolerance. Tolerance remains a fallback when no eligible area contains the point exactly. Lookup labels these matches as exact or tolerance only. This avoids choosing a smaller neighbour near a boundary, but cannot correct inaccurate source polygons. Test affected coordinates in Lookup before changing broader or tighter matching.

It is useful when the app finds the right general area, but chooses the wrong name for your taste. For example:

  • it picks a district instead of the wider city
  • it picks a very small local area instead of the municipality
  • it picks something broader than you want

With newly downloaded Overture country caches, a containing neighborhood can supply its parent city when your preferred city type has no polygon match. Your configured place-type order still applies. The app only uses parent information from an area whose geometry matches the coordinate.

Existing caches continue to work. To use parent matching for a country cached before this update, re-download its Overture cache on the Data page, then compare known coordinates in Lookup before reprocessing your library.

items.title: What it does not change
items.text:
The City Resolver does not download better data or invent missing places.

It will not help if:

  • the place you want is not in the Lookup results at all
  • the airport name is winning and airport matching is still turned on
  • the country match is wrong

So before changing anything, use Lookup first and make sure the place you want is actually in the returned data.

items.title: Recommended workflow
items.text:
1. Open the Lookup page and test a coordinate that gave you a bad city result.
  2. Look at Resolved City, Raw Best Area, and the candidate list.
  3. If the place you want is present, decide what to change:
  4. if the wrong kind of place won, change the preferred order
  5. if two similar places are competing, try broader or tighter matching
  6. if an airport name is winning, turn off airport matching first
  7. Add a country override only after you know the data supports the result you want.
  8. Run Lookup again and confirm the final output before processing your library.

items.title: About admin_level
items.text:
Lookup shows admin_level because it can sometimes help explain why a result was chosen, but it is not a setting you edit directly.

That is because:

  • many results do not have a useful admin_level
  • the place type is usually more important than the number
  • admin_level alone does not solve every case

So the controls on the City Resolver page stay simple:

  • preferred place type order
  • broader or tighter matching

items.title: Bundled defaults vs your overrides
items.text:
The bundled US profile tries county names after all its city-like place types. For example, a coordinate without a city match can resolve to Monroe County, Florida rather than Florida, Florida. A matching airport boundary can still override that name when airport matching is enabled. This does not add missing towns, parks, or islands to the source data.

Your explicit global or US override can replace that order. To keep county as a fallback, add county last in your preferred place types. Check representative coordinates in Lookup before saving a custom order. Existing Immich names are not changed automatically; start a new scan in Location Management to review proposals using the saved settings.

The app ships with built-in default rules. Your own settings sit on top of them:

  • bundled global default
  • bundled country-specific default, if present
  • your optional global override
  • your optional country override

That means you only need to change the countries you care about.

items.title: Want to improve the bundled defaults for everyone?
items.text:
If you find a country setting that clearly works better, you can open a pull request.

The bundled defaults currently live in:

  • src/ImmichReverseGeo.Web/bundled-data/defaults/city-resolver-profiles.json

A good pull request should include:

  • the country ISO3 code
  • one or more example coordinates
  • the old result
  • the new expected result
  • a short explanation of why the new default is better
  • Lookup evidence showing that the desired place is really in the returned data

See the contributor notes in CONTRIBUTING.md.

items.title: Database connection details
items.text:
The database section in Settings is read-only and mainly there as a sanity check.

  • values are taken from the running process environment
  • they are not stored in settings.json

items.title: Data layout
items.text:
Runtime data goes under /data.

Config goes under /config in production.

items.title: Operational notes
items.text:
Turn off immich’s built-in reverse geocoding

Only one tool should be updating location names. See immich’s Reverse Geocoding Settings.

Geo resets are a real change

The Reset Immich Geo Data page under Data can reset reverse geo country, state, and city values for all assets, pasted asset GUIDs, or a selected location value before a rerun, so a database backup is strongly recommended first.

Country downloads take space

The app needs internet access when a country is downloaded for the first time, and those downloads can grow over time.

Do not run two reverse-geocoders against the same immich library

Immich ReverseGeo should be the only tool updating your immich location fields.

Turn off immich's built-in reverse geocoding before using this app, otherwise the two systems can step on each other's results. See immich's official docs: Reverse Geocoding and Reverse Geocoding Settings.

Clearing location data is a real metadata change

The Reset Immich Geo Data page does not just reset this app's local state. It can clear existing immich reverse geo city, state, and country fields in the database.

It does not touch any other immich metadata.

Take a database backup before using it: Backup and Restore | Immich

items.title: Data Sources
items.text:
This page explains the geographic data sources Immich ReverseGeo uses today, where they come from, why the app uses them, and what license limits matter in practice.

Use this page when you want to answer questions like:

  • what data is built into the app image
  • what data is downloaded later on demand
  • why one source is used for country matching while another is used for state or city matching
  • whether a source is suitable for your setup

items.title: At a glance
items.text: Source How the app uses it Built in or downloaded License notes Built-in Overture country data Country matching Built in ODbL Downloaded Overture administrative caches State matching, city matching Downloaded per country on demand ODbL Built-in airport data Airport-area matching Built in ODbL Optional live Overture Places diagnostics Extra Lookup diagnostics only Live query during Lookup when enabled Multi-license dataset, varies by source Optional GADM administrative data Optional administrative fallback or preferred admin source Downloaded per country on demand Non-commercial use only

items.title: Built-in Overture country data
items.text:
Immich ReverseGeo ships with a small bundled Overture country cache.

A separate bundled country catalog provides standard codes and display names for country selection lists. It can translate supported Overture source aliases into standard identities, but it does not supply geographic boundaries or add coverage. Use Lookup to check whether a coordinate matches the bundled country data.

The app uses it for:

  • the first country match for a coordinate
  • deciding which country-specific admin cache should be loaded next
  • letting Lookup work immediately without waiting for the first country-level download

Why this source is used:

  • it is open and easy to bundle
  • it gives consistent country and distinct-territory boundaries for the active runtime
  • it avoids a live network dependency for the first step of every lookup
  • territories keep their own ISO identity instead of being rewritten as the administering country

The bundled fixture set covers Hong Kong, Macao, Greenland, the Faroe Islands, Jersey, Guernsey, the Isle of Man, Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Bermuda, Gibraltar, the Cayman Islands, the British Virgin Islands, Aruba, Curaçao, the Åland Islands, Réunion, French Polynesia, and New Caledonia.

What it does not do by itself:

  • it is not the main state and city source for the final result
  • a territory outside the bundled fixture set can still be missing if the pinned Overture release has no country or dependency boundary for it
  • changing the bundled database requires an application or container restart because the country index stays in memory

Older custom country databases remain usable for country codes the catalog recognizes; the app does not rewrite those files. They retain their original geographic coverage. A missing or conflicting country identity in a newer-format database is reported as a mapping error rather than being assigned to a nearby country.

Country coverage does not guarantee city or state coverage. Optional GADM data can be unavailable for an identity; the app then keeps available Overture results. Updating the app does not automatically replace existing Immich location names. Use Location Management to scan and review proposed corrections before applying them.

If a coordinate still looks wrong, use Lookup first. Confirm the country identity, then inspect the downloaded Overture and optional GADM administrative results before changing settings.

Origin:

  • Overture Maps divisions theme, especially division_area

License:

  • ODbL for the divisions theme

Official references:

  • Overture Divisions Guide
  • Overture Attribution and Licensing

items.title: Downloaded Overture administrative caches
items.text:
When the app needs better state and city matching, it downloads a per-country Overture administrative cache into /data/overture-divisions/{ISO3}.db.

Downloads include separate Overture source codes for Saba, Sint Eustatius, Clipperton Island, and Jan Mayen in their corresponding country caches. Older affected caches refresh automatically the next time they are needed. This improves downloaded boundary coverage; it does not add boundaries or names missing from Overture. Use Lookup on a known coordinate to check the state and city result before processing your library. Country detection must also recognize the location before normal processing can use its cache.

New caches also include parent-area information. This can recover a city from a matching neighborhood and keep the selected city and state in the same administrative hierarchy. It cannot invent a missing city or correct an inaccurate boundary. Other older caches remain usable; re-download an individual country on the Data page to gain parent matching, and validate the result in Lookup first.

The app uses this source for:

  • normal administrative area matching during processing
  • the default state and city result in Lookup
  • the baseline admin result even when optional GADM support is enabled

Why this source is used:

  • it is a strong open default
  • it is shaped for containment checks like reverse geocoding
  • per-country caching keeps local storage more manageable than downloading the whole world

What it does not do:

  • it does not guarantee that every municipality or territory is represented the way you expect
  • it does not guarantee current legal or official naming in every country

Origin:

  • Overture Maps divisions theme

License:

  • ODbL for the divisions theme

Official references:

  • Overture Divisions Guide
  • Overture Attribution and Licensing

items.title: Built-in airport data
items.text:
Immich ReverseGeo also ships with a bundled airport-focused extract built from Overture data.

The extract uses Overture release 2026-09-23.1. Airports may be represented by a boundary or only a point, so the data cannot always establish whether a photo was taken on airport grounds. Updating the app supplies the new bundled extract; it does not replace existing Immich location names. Use Lookup to check known coordinates, then Location Management to review and apply selected corrections.

The app uses it for:

  • recognizing airport grounds more accurately than a normal city or commune lookup
  • optionally overriding the city name when the point is clearly inside an airport geometry
  • helping airport photos resolve to the airport itself when that is the more useful label

Why this source is used:

  • airport photos are a common case where plain admin boundaries feel wrong
  • keeping the airport extract bundled avoids another first-run download for this feature

What it does not do:

  • it is not a general-purpose places database
  • by default, point-only airports, missing or invalid boundaries, and coordinates more than 5 m outside an airport boundary are excluded
  • the optional point-only fallback can fill an empty city within 100 m, but cannot confirm airport grounds or replace an administrative city/county
  • proximity and bounding-box overlap alone do not confirm airport grounds

Origin:

  • exported from the Overture base theme's infrastructure data, derived from OpenStreetMap

License:

  • ODbL for this OpenStreetMap-derived extract

Official references:

  • Overture Infrastructure Guide
  • Overture Attribution and Licensing

items.title: Optional live Overture Places diagnostics
items.text:
Enable Include nearby places on the Lookup page to investigate a coordinate. The app shows up to five nearby suggestions with distance, category, operating status, existence confidence, sources, and the reason they were included. Lookup Trace lists all returned candidates.

Suggestions are filtered before the result limit and ordered by distance within 2.5 km. Broad sports or transportation categories do not automatically qualify as useful places. The app returns at most 80 suggestions and a separate sample of up to 20 nearest excluded places, with reasons such as low or unknown confidence, closure, or an unsuitable category. The excluded sample is not a complete list of nearby places.

Existence confidence estimates whether a place exists; it does not measure whether your photo was taken there. Overture Places are points, so proximity does not prove that a coordinate is inside a museum, park, or other venue. These results are for investigation and never replace the city, state, or country written to Immich.

The app uses it for:

  • helping you inspect whether a nearby place or point of interest exists in Overture
  • debugging difficult coordinates where the administrative result is not enough

Why this source is optional:

  • it is slower than bundled or cached local sources
  • it depends on live access to Overture-hosted public data
  • it is useful for investigation, but not required for normal processing

What it does not do:

  • it is not the default source for the city written back to Immich
  • it is not required for normal country, state, or city processing

Origin:

  • Overture Maps places theme

License:

  • Overture Places is a multi-license dataset
  • license terms depend on the source of each place record
  • current source licenses listed by Overture include CC0-1.0, Apache-2.0, and CDLA-Permissive-2.0

Official references:

  • Overture Places Guide
  • Overture Attribution and Licensing

items.title: Optional GADM administrative data
items.text:
GADM is an optional source for administrative boundaries.

When enabled, the app downloads one or more country GeoPackages and builds local caches under /data/gadm-divisions/{ISO3}.db.

The app uses it for:

  • optional state and city matching in Lookup
  • optional fallback or preferred admin matching during processing
  • some cases where a traditional admin-boundary dataset gives a better municipality or state result than Overture

Why this source is optional instead of the default:

  • its license is much more restrictive than Overture
  • it can involve large country downloads
  • it still depends on the bundled Overture country match to decide which country cache to try first

What it can fix:

  • some cases where Overture admin naming or municipality choice is not ideal
  • some split-territory cases when the detected country is expanded through the app's GADM fallback family rules

What it cannot fix:

  • cases where the initial bundled country lookup finds no country at all
  • all territory or sovereignty edge cases
  • commercial-use licensing concerns

Origin:

  • GADM country packages in GeoPackage format

License:

  • GADM says the data is for academic and other non-commercial use
  • redistribution or commercial use is not allowed without prior permission

Practical meaning for this project:

  • fine for non-commercial use
  • not a clean fit for commercial use
  • still worth testing with Lookup before enabling it for full-library processing

Official references:

  • GADM About
  • GADM Data
  • GADM License

items.title: Why there is more than one source
items.text:
No single source is best at everything.

Immich ReverseGeo mixes sources on purpose:

  • bundled Overture country data gives a fast local first step
  • downloaded Overture admin data is the open default for state and city matching
  • bundled airport data helps where an airport name is more useful than the surrounding municipality
  • optional GADM can improve some admin-boundary cases
  • optional live Overture Places helps you inspect difficult coordinates before changing settings

That also means there is no promise that every source will agree with every other source for every point.

The recommended workflow is:

  1. test a coordinate in Lookup
  2. compare the returned sources
  3. decide whether you want default Overture behavior, airport matching, or optional GADM for that use case

items.title: Storage and network behavior
items.text:
• built-in Overture country and airport data ships inside the app image
  • low-memory country lookups prepare a regenerable polygon index under /data/country-polygon-parts.db, without downloading or changing the bundled data
  • downloaded Overture and GADM country caches are stored under /data
  • if a downloaded cache disappears or its file size or timestamps change, the app checks it again before reuse; missing or unusable caches are recreated when needed. Use the Country Caches page to manage downloads, then verify restored data in Lookup
  • new Overture downloads discover the current release from its public catalog; if discovery fails, the app reports an error instead of trying an expired release
  • the first lookup or processing pass for a new country may take longer because the cache must be created locally
  • larger countries can use hundreds of megabytes of local storage per cached country

items.title: Notes
items.text:
This page is a practical summary, not legal advice.

If license terms are important for your deployment, check the official source pages above before enabling or redistributing any optional data path.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text:
This is the fastest end-user path to a first working setup with Docker.

Use Immich ReverseGeo when you want more accurate or more useful location names in immich than the default built-in reverse-geocoding results are giving you.

What is different here is that Immich ReverseGeo uses better location data and more careful matching than immich's built-in reverse geocoding. That usually gives better results for things like coastlines, islands, airport areas, and other places where the default result feels too broad or inaccurate.

Disable immich's built-in reverse geocoding first

Immich ReverseGeo and immich's own reverse geocoding both write location fields.

If both are enabled at the same time, they can overwrite each other's values and cause inconsistent results.

Turn off immich's built-in reverse geocoding before you start processing with Immich ReverseGeo. See immich's official docs: Reverse Geocoding and Reverse Geocoding Settings.

Back up immich before processing or clearing location data

Immich ReverseGeo writes city, state, and country values back into immich's database.

Before processing, applying location corrections, or clearing existing location fields, create a proper immich database backup first.

Follow the official guide: Backup and Restore | Immich

items.title: 1. Make sure you can reach the immich database
items.text:
Immich ReverseGeo needs direct access to the same database your immich instance uses.

In Docker setups, that usually means:

  • joining the same Docker network as immich
  • passing the immich database connection values through to this container

Typical variables:

DB_HOSTNAME=database
DB_PORT=5432
DB_USERNAME=...
DB_PASSWORD=...
DB_DATABASE_NAME=immich

Existing DB_HOST settings remain supported and take precedence over DB_HOSTNAME when nonblank. If neither has a nonblank value, the host defaults to database.

items.title: 2. Start the container
items.text:
Use Docker with persistent mounts for:

  • /config for settings
  • /data for downloaded country data

Add the service to your existing Immich Compose file. See Installation for the snippet or a separate-stack setup.

docker compose up -d immich-reversegeo

items.title: 3. Open the UI
items.text:
Default container URL:

http://localhost:8080
Which computer does localhost refer to?

localhost means the computer running your browser. If Docker runs on another machine, use a private connection to that machine, such as the SSH tunnel below.

If port 8080 is already in use on your host, change the left side of the compose port mapping and open that port instead.

If the container runs on a remote server, do not expose the UI publicly. Docker-published ports can bypass host firewall rules such as UFW. For a VPS, bind the published port to localhost and use SSH local port forwarding, a VPN, or a trusted reverse proxy with authentication:

ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:8080 user@host

items.title: 4. Test one coordinate
items.text:
Use the Lookup page to confirm the basics before a full run:

Country matching

Make sure the country is detected correctly for a coordinate you know well.

State and city matching

Check that the result is reasonably precise and not too broad or generic.

Airport areas

If you have airport photos, confirm they resolve the way you would expect.

items.title: 5. Start manual processing
items.text:
After checking known coordinates in Lookup, use Run Now from the Dashboard for your first manual pass. A smaller batch size reduces work per batch; it does not limit the total number of assets in the run. Inspect the resulting location names in Immich and use Cancel if you need to stop processing.

Processing selects GPS-tagged assets only when both the city and country are missing (stored as NULL in the database). Assets with an existing city or country are not selected, even if the other value is missing.

items.title: Correct existing location names
items.text:
Use Scan & Review Existing Names on the Dashboard to open Location Management. Scanning compares existing names with proposed names without changing Immich.

  1. Start with a few asset GUIDs or one existing location before scanning the whole library.
  2. Review the differences and use Inspect in Lookup to check unfamiliar results. A spelling or punctuation difference does not necessarily mean a better location.
  3. Select the differences you want, open Review Selected Changes, and check the exact names. After taking a database backup, acknowledge the confirmation and choose Confirm Apply.
  4. Refresh those assets in Immich to check the result. Applying writes the reviewed names directly; no reset or processing run is needed.

You can reopen completed results in Saved Scans and inspect applied changes or review an undo in Change History. See Location Management for continuation, filters, and undo limits.

For the advanced reset-and-reprocess workflow, use Reset Selected Assets or Reset by Existing Location on Reset Immich Geo Data, then select Run Now. Reset clears all three location fields—city, state, and country—for the selected assets. See Maintenance actions before confirming.

For more on the UI after setup, see Using the App.

items.title: Docker
items.text:
If you already run immich with Docker Compose, the simplest setup is to add one service to that existing compose file.

Database backup strongly recommended

This service updates immich metadata in the database.

Before first use, and especially before using any bulk-clear action from the Data page, create a proper immich database backup.

Official guide: Backup and Restore | Immich

items.title: Choose your Compose setup
items.text:
Existing Immich stack (recommended)Separate Compose stack

Add the service and volume declarations below to your existing Immich Compose file. Reuse its .env file and default network. Keep /config and /data persisted separately.

docker-compose.yml
# docker-compose.yml
# Add this service to your existing Immich docker-compose.yml.
services:
  immich-reversegeo:
    image: ghcr.io/immich-reversegeo/immich-reversegeo:latest
    container_name: immich-reversegeo
    pull_policy: always
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"          # change the left side if 8080 is already in use; do NOT expose publicly
    volumes:
      - reversegeo-config:/config      # settings (no database secrets in settings.json)
      - reversegeo-data:/data          # Overture caches, skipped.db, runtime data
    env_file:
      - .env                 # reuse Immich's own .env (DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD, etc.)
    environment:
      - ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080
      # Optional photo previews and original-photo links:
      # - IMMICH_URL=http://immich-server:2283
      # - IMMICH_WEB_URL=https://photos.example.com
      # - IMMICH_API_KEY=${REVERSEGEO_IMMICH_API_KEY}
    mem_limit: 2g
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  reversegeo-config:
  reversegeo-data:

Start only Immich ReverseGeo:

docker compose up -d immich-reversegeo

Save the same service snippet in a separate directory and provide an .env file with your Immich database connection values. Join the existing Immich network by adding this section to that Compose file:

networks:
  default:
    external: true
    name: immich_default

Replace immich_default with your actual Immich network name. The database hostname must be reachable on that network. You can inspect available networks with docker network ls.

docker compose up -d immich-reversegeo

Reference file: docker-compose.yml.

Both setups need about 2 GB of memory, as set by mem_limit in the service snippet.

Why the memory limit is there

The bundled country boundary data is held in memory while processing runs and uses several hundred megabytes. mem_limit sets a total container memory budget that the .NET runtime can take into account. Large country caches and high parallelism can increase peak memory use.

Do not lower it much below 2g. A limit under the working set makes the container fail immediately instead of running. Raising it is fine.

Both setups need the database connection values from Immich:

DB_HOSTNAME=database
DB_PORT=5432
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=...
DB_DATABASE_NAME=immich

Use DB_HOSTNAME from Immich's .env file, including when connecting to an external database. A nonblank DB_HOST takes precedence over DB_HOSTNAME for existing installations. If DB_HOST is empty or contains only spaces, the app uses DB_HOSTNAME. If neither has a nonblank value, the host defaults to database.

The example publishes the UI on host port 8080. Change the left side of the port mapping if it is already in use. Do not expose the UI publicly; see the private-access options below.

items.title: Image versions
items.text:
latest normally follows GitHub's designated latest stable release after its image is successfully published. Maintainers can explicitly promote another validated build using the manual publishing option. Use a published version tag to control upgrades, for example ghcr.io/immich-reversegeo/immich-reversegeo:1.2.3. This is an example; choose an available version from GitHub Releases.

  • Releases tagged v1.2.3 publish both 1.2.3 and v1.2.3 image tags.
  • Other stable releases retain their version tags without changing latest. Rerunning an older release does not automatically move latest backwards.
  • Prereleases publish their full version tags, such as 1.2.3-rc.1, without updating latest.
  • edge follows development builds from master after the build, tests, and Docker build checks pass.
  • sha-... tags identify builds by commit.

After changing the image version in your Compose file, run docker compose pull immich-reversegeo and docker compose up -d immich-reversegeo. Keep your existing /config and /data volumes.

items.title: VPS and firewall notes
items.text:
Do not expose the web UI publicly. Docker-published ports can bypass host firewall rules such as UFW, so do not rely on the host firewall alone to hide a broadly published 8080:8080 mapping on an internet-facing server.

If you run Immich ReverseGeo on a VPS and only need local or SSH-forwarded access, bind the published port to localhost:

ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
  # - "[::1]:8080:8080"

Then use a private path such as SSH local port forwarding, a VPN, or a trusted reverse proxy with authentication:

ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:8080 user@host

Then open:

http://localhost:8080

items.title: Runtime notes
items.text:
• Built-in data covers country matching and airport matching.
  • More detailed country data is downloaded only when needed.
  • The app needs internet access the first time it downloads data for a new country.
  • Large countries can use hundreds of megabytes each under /data.

items.title: After install
items.text:
• Use Configuration for database and processing settings.
  • Use Using the App for manual runs, coordinate testing, and reset tools.

items.title: Privacy
items.text:
Immich ReverseGeo is a self-hosted project intended to run in your own environment.

Operationally:

  • asset coordinates are read from your immich database
  • resolved place names are written back to your immich database
  • bundled and cached data is stored locally on your system
  • preview reports save asset GUIDs, coordinates, existing and proposed names, and processing settings locally in your /data volume; they remain until you delete the saved report

The app UI uses local system fonts and does not request fonts from an external provider.

If photo previews are configured, Immich ReverseGeo fetches thumbnails from your Immich server when you view preview results. The API key stays on the server; thumbnail requests are limited to assets in saved preview reports. Image files are not added to the saved reports.

The optional Nearby Places investigation tool on the Lookup page may contact Overture-hosted public data sources when enabled.

You are responsible for how and where you deploy the service.

items.title: Support
items.text:
For bugs, feature ideas, or questions:

  • open an issue in the GitHub repository
  • include coordinates, expected result, and actual result when reporting lookup problems
  • include relevant log lines when reporting processing failures

Helpful details:

  • exact coordinate tested
  • whether the issue was in Lookup or full processing
  • whether the country cache was already present
  • whether the app was running locally or in Docker

Use Copy as Markdown above a guide's heading to copy its text into a support conversation. The Markdown documentation index links to exported setup, guide, and help pages. Review any logs or configuration details before sharing them.
